coverage: The final focused test uses the actual App route table, ExperienceUtilities Help Link, React Router navigation, and Radix Dialog. It asserts the original textarea DOM node/value and pathname, search, and hash remain mounted while Help is open, then verifies return navigation and focus to the actual Help link.

The work textarea and support page content are test fixtures; this proves generic mounted-route DOM preservation, not a production task composer draft, its crash recovery, or an authenticated API journey.

A same-session unsettled recheck keeps the underlying node mounted but hidden. Session or selected-company mismatch drops the background route. A direct support deep link renders standalone without a dialog.

Support navigation state carries the company/user binding, background key, return path, and existing allowlisted context; the originating location is retained in memory by App. No task body or permission data is copied into support navigation state.
